title: Deploying AI from pilot to production
subtitle: This guide by Anthropic and Accenture shares seven considerations for taking enterprise AI from pilot to production, and the decisions leadership needs to make before the program advances.

blocks.text: A successful AI pilot doesn’t guarantee successful deployment to the rest of an organization. According to Accenture’s Pulse of Change report (July 2026), only 23% of C-suite leaders report having achieved sustained, enterprise-wide impact with AI initiatives.
blocks.html: A successful AI pilot doesn’t guarantee successful deployment to the rest of an organization. According to Accenture’s Pulse of Change report (July 2026), only 23% of C-suite leaders report having achieved sustained, enterprise-wide impact with AI initiatives.

blocks.text: Pilots are designed for success. Teams are handpicked, often selected for enthusiasm and capability, and work on a defined scope with clear timelines. Pilot budgets are often protected, with insulation from normal organizational dynamics. This makes pilots unrepresentative of the conditions under which AI programs run in production.
blocks.html: Pilots are designed for success. Teams are handpicked, often selected for enthusiasm and capability, and work on a defined scope with clear timelines. blocks.text: Accenture’s September 2026 Tokenomics research found that 42% of organizations rely on shared IT and finance accountability, with no single owner responsible for AI costs and outcomes. Without that owner, it becomes difficult to measure success, make tradeoffs, and maintain accountability as an AI program scales.

blocks.text: To help CIOs and technical leaders get AI programs from pilot into production, we worked with Accenture to put together a practical blueprint. It draws on what we’ve observed in enterprise deployments built on Claude and what Accenture has seen in the implementations it has guided across industries and geographies.
